en.title: Index Pairs Whose Sum Is Divisible by N
en.description:
Count the index pairs with i<j such that a[i]+a[j] is divisible by N. Elements with duplicate values still have distinct identities, and an element cannot be paired with itself.

This site independently compiled the standard I/O and the solution; additions for bounds missing from the source and corrections to the examples are stated explicitly in the protocol.
en.input: The first line contains the array length n and the divisor N, and the second line contains n numbers. Complete original bounds: 1≤n≤100000, 1≤N≤10^9, 1≤a[i]≤10^9; output a 64-bit integer.
en.explanation: The first example has 4 pairs: original indices (0,1), (0,4), (1,3), and (3,4). The original explanation reversed the array without updating the indices accordingly; this site corrects it. The other two examples give 3 and 0.
hints: Scan the remainders in order, using a dictionary to record the frequencies of earlier remainders; add the count of the complementary remainder, then add the current element.
